title: 3rd Truth With The Verses Of Resurrection The Ease Of Resurrection By A Single Command

questions.question: What action does the passage say Allah carries out through His command of creation?
questions.answer: He restores the earth to life.

questions.question: According to the passage, how are people and jinn brought to the place of resurrection?
questions.answer: They are brought together by one command, described as a single cry.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about how long resurrection and gathering will take?
questions.answer: It will happen extremely quickly, in less time than a blink or about that fast.

questions.question: In the passage, what comparison is made to show the ease of creating and resurrecting all people?
questions.answer: Bringing all of them into being again is said to be as easy as bringing one soul into being.

questions.question: Which groups besides human beings are mentioned as being gathered at the Supreme Gathering?
questions.answer: Jinn, animals, spirit beings, and angels are also mentioned.

questions.question: What is meant by saying one concern does not interfere with another?
questions.answer: Handling countless beings at once causes no difficulty or distraction for Allah.

questions.question: What main idea ties the three cited verses together in this passage?
questions.answer: They all show that resurrection for all creatures is easy, swift, and done by Allah’s single command.

questions.question: Based on the passage, why is the resurrection of every creature not presented as a difficult task?
questions.answer: Because Allah’s power reaches all of them together with complete ease.

questions.question: How does the passage end its discussion of these mysteries?
questions.answer: It says the later mysteries, from the third to the thirteenth, are delayed until another time.

questions.question: What happens to the earth through Allah’s creative order in this passage?
questions.answer: It is revived and brought back to life.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the call that gathers creation for resurrection?
questions.answer: It describes it as one call that brings them all into Allah’s presence.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the speed of the Last Hour and the gathering after it?
questions.answer: It teaches that both will occur with amazing speed, faster than people would normally imagine.

questions.question: How is the resurrection of all people compared with the resurrection of one individual?
questions.answer: There is no difference in difficulty; both are equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: Who will be assembled in the field of the Supreme Gathering according to the passage?
questions.answer: Human beings, jinn, animals, spiritual creatures, and angels.

questions.question: What does the phrase about a single command show about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah does not need many separate actions to gather all creation.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention both creation and resurrection together?
questions.answer: To show that giving life the first time and bringing it back again are both easy for Allah.

questions.question: What can a student infer from the statement that one matter does not disturb another?
questions.answer: Allah’s care for one creature never prevents Him from dealing perfectly with all others.

questions.question: What is the central message of this target passage?
questions.answer: The resurrection of all creatures is certain, immediate by Allah’s command, and effortless for Him.

questions.question: What note does the speaker add about the later mysteries?
questions.answer: He says they have been postponed, even though he is not pleased about delaying them.

questions.question: At the beginning of the passage, what result comes from Allah’s command of creation?
questions.answer: The earth is made alive again.

questions.question: What is the effect of the single cry mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: It gathers all people and jinn and brings them forward together.

questions.question: How does the image of a blink help explain resurrection?
questions.answer: It shows that the event will happen with extreme quickness.

questions.question: What lesson is taught by the statement that all people are like one soul in creation and resurrection?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is not strained by large numbers, so all humanity is no harder than one person.

questions.question: Name two non-human groups the passage says will also be gathered.
questions.answer: Any two of these are correct: jinn, animals, spirit beings, or angels.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the scope of the final gathering?
questions.answer: It includes many different kinds of creatures, not only human beings.

questions.question: How do the three verses work together in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: One shows the single command, another shows the speed, and the third shows the equal ease of many and one.

questions.question: If someone thinks raising all creation is too much at once, how does the passage answer that idea?
questions.answer: It says that for Allah, many tasks do not clash or create any difficulty.

questions.question: What is postponed according to the final sentence of the target passage?
questions.answer: The discussion of the remaining mysteries, from the third through the thirteenth.

questions.question: What does the passage say Allah does to the earth by His command?
questions.answer: He revives it.

questions.question: In the passage, what gathers all people and jinn to the place of resurrection?
questions.answer: One divine call or command gathers them.

questions.question: What does the passage teach by comparing resurrection to the movement of an eye?
questions.answer: It teaches that resurrection and the following gathering will happen very rapidly.

questions.question: What does the statement about one soul teach about Allah’s relation to all people?
questions.answer: The number of people does not make the act harder for Him.

questions.question: Which beings are said to be brought to the field of the Supreme Gathering?
questions.answer: All human beings and jinn, along with animals, spirit beings, and angels.

questions.question: What does “with great ease” tell us about the nature of this gathering?
questions.answer: It shows that the event is effortless for Allah despite its vast scale.

questions.question: Why is it important in the passage that one concern does not interfere with another?
questions.answer: It emphasizes that Allah can deal with every creature fully at the same time.

questions.question: What overall belief about the Hereafter is strengthened by this passage?
questions.answer: It strengthens belief that the final resurrection will truly happen and will be easy for Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage combine certainty and power in its description of resurrection?
questions.answer: It presents resurrection as a definite event carried out by Allah’s command without delay or difficulty.

questions.question: How does the passage close after discussing these verses?
questions.answer: It closes by saying the rest of the mysteries will be explained later.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens to the earth through Allah’s creative command?
questions.answer: It comes back to life.

questions.question: How are all people and jinn said to be summoned on the Day of Resurrection?
questions.answer: They are summoned together by one cry and one command.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying the Hour is like a blink or even nearer?
questions.answer: The final event and what follows it will occur almost instantly.

questions.question: In what way is humanity’s creation and resurrection compared to a single soul?
questions.answer: The whole of humanity is as easy for Allah to create and raise as one individual.

questions.question: Besides humans and jinn, what other creatures are included in the final assembly?
questions.answer: Animals, spirit beings, and angels.

questions.question: What can we understand from the words “single command”?
questions.answer: Allah’s will is enough to gather all creation at once.

questions.question: What idea about divine ability is repeated across the quoted verses?
questions.answer: Allah’s power acts quickly, completely, and without being limited by number.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the field of the Supreme Gathering and the great balance together?
questions.answer: To show that resurrection leads into a universal assembly and just reckoning.

questions.question: What misunderstanding does the line about one concern not interfering with another correct?
questions.answer: It corrects the thought that managing many beings at once would divide or weaken divine power.

questions.question: What feeling does the speaker express about delaying the later mysteries?
questions.answer: He indicates personal dislike for having to postpone them.

questions.question: What first example of revival is given before the verses about resurrection are explained?
questions.answer: The earth being brought back to life.

questions.question: What does the passage say will bring all people and jinn into divine presence?
questions.answer: A single call and command will bring them all there.

questions.question: How fast does the passage say resurrection and gathering will be?
questions.answer: They will happen with the speed of a blink, or even faster.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the comparison between all people and one soul?
questions.answer: For Allah, raising everyone is no more difficult than raising one person.

questions.question: What full range of beings does the passage say will be gathered?
questions.answer: Human beings, jinn, animals, spiritual beings, and angels.

questions.question: What does the statement that one matter does not hinder another reveal about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It reveals that Allah’s power is unlimited and not overburdened by many simultaneous acts.

questions.question: How does the passage build its case for the ease of resurrection?
questions.answer: It uses three verses to show one command, extreme speed, and equal ease between one and all.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about the scale of the final gathering?
questions.answer: It will be universal, including many kinds of created beings together.

questions.question: What is the strongest main idea a student should take from this passage?
questions.answer: The complete resurrection and gathering of creation is easy and certain by Allah’s command.

questions.question: What information is given about the mysteries after the second one?
questions.answer: Their explanation is put off until later, from the third mystery through the thirteenth.
